Rendering rides the already-PG-verified formatInterval time component. Tests: internal/executor/interval_subday_test.go TestSubDayIntervalLiterals. Follow-ups since RESOLVED (all landed): fractional magnitudes (2026-07-11), multi-field / HH:MM:SS literals (2026-07-11, hoisted the interval-body math into internal/parser/interval.go ParseIntervalBody), the coarse units week/decade/century/millennium/microsecond incl. dec/cent/mil/us/usec abbreviations (2026-07-11, canonicalIntervalUnit + IntervalUnitToParts; tests TestWeekDecadeCenturyIntervals), and the bare-number default-unit d-i (2026-07-11, a unitless field defaults to seconds: interval '5' -> 00:00:05, interval '1 day 5' -> 1 day 00:00:05; ParseIntervalBody accepts a unitless number only as the final field with the SECOND slot free, reproducing PG DecodeInterval's right-to-left tmask&fmask collision rule so interval '1 2 days'/'5 5'/'1 day 05:00:00 5' still error; tests TestTrailingBareNumberDefaultsToSeconds), and the SQL year-month hyphen field (2026-07-11, interval '1-2' -> 1 year 2 months: a <int>-<int> token decodes to years*12 +/- months via new parser.parseYearMonthField, mirroring PG DecodeInterval's DTK_NUMBER hyphen branch type=DTK_MONTH; leading '-' flips both year and month sign so '-1-2' -> -14 months; month part bounded 0<=m<12 with nothing trailing so '1-12'/'1-13'/'1--2'/'1-2-3'/'1-2x' error; composes with other fields incl. trailing bare-seconds '1-2 3' -> 1 year 2 mons 00:00:03; tests TestYearMonthHyphenIntervals), and the single-letter unit forms d-ii (2026-07-11, y/c/w/d/h/m/s added to canonicalIntervalUnit from PG's deltatktbl; in an interval literal m is unambiguously MINUTE not month -- DecodeInterval decodes the unit via DecodeUnits->deltatktbl regardless of neighbouring fields, so there is no positional ambiguity: interval '1 m' -> 00:01:00 and interval '1 y 2 m' -> 1 year 00:02:00; quarter/qtr and the timezone tokens (tz/timezone) appear in deltatktbl but have no case in DecodeInterval's per-unit switch so PG raises DTERR_BAD_FORMAT 22007 and goopg intentionally rejects them too; tests TestWeekDecadeCenturyIntervals + TestIntervalCastFromStringInvalidSyntax), and the glued <magnitude><unit> forms plus field-mask collisions d-iii (2026-07-11, interval '2h30m'/'1.5h'/'1y2mon3d'/'-5h'/'1day' now parse: ParseIntervalBody pre-expands each whitespace field via expandIntervalFields/splitAlphaNumRuns, reproducing PG ParseDateTime's digit<->letter field split incl. the datetktbl gobble rule -- a multi-letter unit glued before a digit is accepted only when the letters form an absolute datetktbl token (d/h/m/s/y/mon/dec) so '1d2h'/'1mon2d'/'1dec2d' parse but '1day2h'/'1w2d'/'1min2sec' error; and the DecodeInterval tmask&fmask collision check is now modelled by an intervalFieldMask so repeated fields error -- '1h2h', '1 mon 2 mons', '1-2 3 mons', a unit colliding with a HH:MM:SS time word '1h 05:00:00', and fractional-second-vs-ms '1.5 sec 200 ms' all raise 22007; tests TestGluedIntervalLiterals), and the ISO-8601 duration bodies d-iii-rest (2026-07-11, interval 'P1Y2M3DT4H5M6S'/'PT1H30M'/'P1.5D' plus the alternative format extended 'P0002-06-07T01:30:00' and basic packed 'P00020607T013000' now parse: ParseIntervalBody was split into decodeIntervalFields (the free-form decoder) + a new decodeISO8601Interval fallback tried ONLY when the free-form decoder fails, exactly PG interval_in's 'if bad format, try ISO8601 style' ordering; decodeISO8601Interval line-ports DecodeISO8601Interval as a datepart/havefield state machine over P<date>T<time> -- Y/M/W/D before T, H/M/S after so M is months before T but minutes after -- and every designator + extended-alternative field routes through the shared IntervalUnitToParts so the two decoders cannot drift, only the 8-digit/6-digit basic packed formats use inline math; new scanISONumberPrefix/parseISO8601Number/iso8601IntegerWidth/clampISOInterval mirror PG's ParseISO8601Number/ISO8601IntegerWidth/itmin2interval; tests TestISO8601IntervalLiterals), and the year-month tokenizer quirks '1-' and '1-2.5' (2026-07-11: interval '1-' -> 1 year and interval '1-2.5' -> 1 year 2 mons 00:00:00.5. PG's ParseDateTime lexer reads '1-2.5' as a DTK_DATE field '1-2' then a fresh DTK_NUMBER field '.5', so the fraction decodes as seconds; new splitYearMonthFraction in expandIntervalFields peels a '.'-led run off an UNSIGNED <digits>-<digits?> field and feeds the remainder back through splitAlphaNumRuns so '1-2.5day' splits again into .5+day -> +12:00:00. A SIGNED field ('-1-2.5','+1-2.5') is lexed whole as PG's DTK_TZ token whose years-months branch rejects the .5 tail, so goopg leaves it whole and errors too. parseYearMonthField now treats an empty month tail as 0 months ('1-'/'-1-' are bare years, PG strtoint on the empty tail = 0); tests TestYearMonthHyphenIntervals +22 accepts/8 rejects). STILL DEFERRED (see deferral_ledger.md): (d-iii-rest) full interval typmod grammar (HOUR TO MINUTE ranges, SECOND(p) precision, Form-1 trailing-word column-alias fall-through); interval +/- infinity; and a bare unit-word glued to a year-month field (interval '1-2h' -> PG 1 year 2 mons with the 'h' absorbed as a no-op since the year-month forces DTK_MONTH; goopg errors).
